scope: Flare treatment choices in NG219 when first-line drugs are contraindicated, not tolerated, or ineffective.

keyRecommendations.text: Consider an intra-articular or intramuscular corticosteroid if NSAIDs and colchicine are contraindicated, not tolerated, or ineffective.
Do not offer an IL-1 inhibitor unless NSAIDs, colchicine, and corticosteroids are contraindicated, not tolerated, or ineffective, and refer to rheumatology before prescribing it.
Consider a PPI for people taking an NSAID for a flare.
keyRecommendations.population: Gout flare treated with an NSAID

clinicalBottomLine: NG219 steps from an NSAID, colchicine, or oral corticosteroid to an intra-articular or intramuscular corticosteroid, and only then to an IL-1 inhibitor after rheumatology referral. It does not describe intravenous corticosteroid or a colchicine interaction list.
notableCaveats: Questions do not invent clarithromycin, renal-dose colchicine rules, or intravenous steroid doses, because those statements are not in the stored NG219 text.
